Three saved WGCNA networks describe developmental ATAC, H3K27ac and H3K27me3 profiles. Input preparation, quality filtering, soft-threshold diagnostics, network fitting and grey-module refinement are included below. By default, this notebook loads the saved fits and displays their eigengenes; all fitting flags default to false.

Soft powers were 6, 5 and 9, respectively, with signed networks, bicor correlation, signed TOM, minimum module size 30, merge height 0.25, deepSplit 2 and pamStage FALSE. The saved ATAC network contains 67,435 fitted features; the final annotated ATAC catalog contains 67,518 intervals. Initial network colors, final refined labels and plotting transformations are kept distinct, as documented in `pipeline/02_module_annotation.Rmd`.

## Inputs and saved objects

Paths are relative to the `CortexCode/` directory. **saved-results** inputs support routine rendering; **optional-rerun** inputs are read only when the corresponding analysis is enabled. Wildcards identify file collections.

| Mode | Input path | Use |
|---|---|---|
| saved-results | `data/upstream/WGCNA/WGCNA_objects/*.Rds` | Three fitted ATAC, H3K27ac and H3K27me3 networks |
| optional-rerun | `data/upstream/WGCNA/WGCNA_input_data/atac_idr_peaks_merged_uniform-mm10.tsv` | ATAC raw peak-by-sample counts |
| optional-rerun | `data/upstream/WGCNA/WGCNA_input_data/hac_overlap_peaks_merged-mm10.tsv` | H3K27ac raw peak-by-sample counts |
| optional-rerun | `data/upstream/WGCNA/WGCNA_input_data/htk_overlap_peaks_merged-mm10.tsv` | H3K27me3 raw peak-by-sample counts |
| optional-rerun | `data/upstream/final_tables/Supp_Table_[123]*.csv` | Final ATAC, AC and ME3 catalogs for refinement |
| optional-rerun | `data/upstream/Module_renaming_dictionary.csv` | Biological module to manuscript-label mapping |

See [input locations](INPUTS.md), [saved R objects](SAVED_OBJECTS.md) and the [complete file inventory](config/file_inventory.csv) for original source names, sizes and availability. These large inputs are not part of the Git checkout.

## Packages and input locations

The analysis starts from the original peak-count tables. Rerun outputs are written separately from the saved input networks.

```{r wgcna-packages-and-input-locations, eval=isTRUE(params$run_wgcna)}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(
  {
    library(WGCNA)
    library(edgeR)
    library(GenomicRanges)
  }
)
input_dir <- file.path(repo_dir, "data", "upstream", "WGCNA", "WGCNA_input_data")
output_dir <- file.path(repo_dir, "objects", "WGCNA", "recomputed")
dir.create(output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE)
atac_input <- read.table(
  file.path(input_dir, "atac_idr_peaks_merged_uniform-mm10.tsv"),
  header = TRUE
)
ac_input <- read.table(
  file.path(input_dir, "hac_overlap_peaks_merged-mm10.tsv"),
  header = TRUE
)
me3_input <- read.table(
  file.path(input_dir, "htk_overlap_peaks_merged-mm10.tsv"),
  header = TRUE
)
```

## ATAC count matrix

The original ATAC table has four coordinate/summit columns followed by 20 sample-count columns. ATAC intervals are already uniform; this branch does not apply the additional histone-peak merge.

```{r wgcna-atac-count-matrix, eval=isTRUE(params$run_wgcna)}
atac_input$ID <- paste(atac_input$chrom, atac_input$start, atac_input$end, sep = "_")
rownames(atac_input) <- atac_input$ID
atac_counts <- as.matrix(atac_input[, 5:24])
storage.mode(atac_counts) <- "numeric"
```

## Histone intervals within 1 kb

For each histone mark, `reduce(min.gapwidth = 1000)` merges intervals separated by fewer than 1,000 bases. Original peak counts are summed within each merged interval. This is interval consolidation of the existing count table; it does not recall peaks or recount BAM reads. Coordinates are passed to the same GRanges constructor convention used in the source script.

```{r wgcna-histone-intervals-within-1-kb, eval=isTRUE(params$run_wgcna)}
merge_histone_counts <- function(peak_table) {
  count_columns <- 4:ncol(peak_table)
  sample_names <- names(peak_table)[count_columns]

  peak_table[, count_columns] <- lapply(peak_table[, count_columns], as.numeric)

  original_ranges <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(
    peak_table, seqnames.field = names(peak_table)[1],
    start.field = names(peak_table)[2],
    end.field = names(peak_table)[3],
    keep.extra.columns = TRUE
  )
  merged_ranges <- GenomicRanges::reduce(original_ranges, min.gapwidth = 1000)

  original_counts <- as.matrix(peak_table[, count_columns])
  storage.mode(original_counts) <- "numeric"
  overlaps <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(merged_ranges, original_ranges)
  source_rows <- split(
    subjectHits(overlaps),
    queryHits(overlaps)
  )

  merged_counts <- matrix(
    0, nrow = length(merged_ranges),
    ncol = length(sample_names),
    dimnames = list(NULL, sample_names)
  )
  for (interval in names(source_rows)) {
    merged_counts[as.integer(interval),
      ] <- colSums(original_counts[source_rows[[interval]], , drop = FALSE])
  }

  rownames(merged_counts) <- paste(
    as.character(seqnames(merged_ranges)),
    start(merged_ranges),
    end(merged_ranges),
    sep = "_"
  )
  mcols(merged_ranges) <- as.data.frame(merged_counts)

  list(ranges = merged_ranges,
    counts = merged_counts)
}
ac_merged <- merge_histone_counts(ac_input)
me3_merged <- merge_histone_counts(me3_input)
```

## Normalization and quality filtering

The original implementation creates an edgeR DGEList and calls `cpm()` without a separate `calcNormFactors()` step. Thus the WGCNA input is library-size CPM, not log-CPM, FPKM, TMM-adjusted expression or a heatmap z score. Samples form rows and intervals form columns. `goodSamplesGenes()` supplies the retained sample/feature mask. Sample clustering is a diagnostic display; the code does not introduce an additional automatic outlier-removal rule.

```{r wgcna-normalization-and-quality-filtering, eval=isTRUE(params$run_wgcna)}
prepare_wgcna_input <- function(count_matrix) {
  dge <- edgeR::DGEList(counts = count_matrix)
  cpm_matrix <- edgeR::cpm(dge)
  expression_matrix <- t(cpm_matrix)

  quality <- WGCNA::goodSamplesGenes(expression_matrix, verbose = 3)
  if (!quality$allOK) {
    expression_matrix <- expression_matrix[quality$goodSamples, quality$goodGenes,
      drop = FALSE]
  }

  list(expression = expression_matrix,
    quality = quality)
}
atac_prepared <- prepare_wgcna_input(atac_counts)
ac_prepared <- prepare_wgcna_input(ac_merged$counts)
me3_prepared <- prepare_wgcna_input(me3_merged$counts)
sample_tree <- hclust(
  dist(atac_prepared$expression),
  method = "average"
)
plot(sample_tree,
  main = "ATAC sample clustering",
  xlab = "",
  sub = "")
```

## Soft-threshold diagnostics

The recorded diagnostic call evaluates powers 1–10 and 12–20 in steps of two. It does not override the correlation or network defaults of `pickSoftThreshold()`. Preserve that original diagnostic call rather than implying it used the explicit bicor/signed options of the fitted network. The selected powers below are fixed analysis settings, not reselected automatically during reproduction.

```{r wgcna-soft-threshold-diagnostics, eval=isTRUE(params$run_wgcna)}
candidate_powers <- c(1:10, seq(12, 20, by = 2))
atac_soft_threshold <- WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold(atac_prepared$expression,
  powerVector = candidate_powers,
  verbose = 5)
ac_soft_threshold <- WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold(ac_prepared$expression,
  powerVector = candidate_powers,
  verbose = 5)
me3_soft_threshold <- WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold(me3_prepared$expression,
  powerVector = candidate_powers,
  verbose = 5)
```

## Signed network fitting

These are the explicit `blockwiseModules()` settings from the original script. Thread counts are 12, 10 and 12 for ATAC, AC and ME3, respectively. The original calls did not explicitly override the default randomSeed argument; package defaults and the execution environment should therefore be recorded for any new rerun.

```{r wgcna-signed-network-fitting, eval=isTRUE(params$run_wgcna)}
fit_network <- function(expression_matrix, power, threads) {
  WGCNA::blockwiseModules(
    datExpr = as.data.frame(expression_matrix),
    checkMissingData = TRUE,
    power = power,
    networkType = "signed",
    TOMType = "signed",

    corType = "bicor",
    minModuleSize = 30,
    maxBlockSize = 25000,
    mergeCutHeight = 0.25,

    deepSplit = 2,
    pamStage = FALSE,
    reassignThreshold = 1e-10,
    saveTOMs = FALSE,

    nThreads = threads,
    verbose = 3
  )
}
net_atac <- fit_network(atac_prepared$expression,
  power = 6,
  threads = 12)
net_ac <- fit_network(ac_prepared$expression,
  power = 5,
  threads = 10)
net_me3 <- fit_network(me3_prepared$expression,
  power = 9,
  threads = 12)
saveRDS(net_atac, file.path(output_dir, "net_WGCNA_ATAC_sp6.Rds"))
saveRDS(
  net_ac, file.path(output_dir, "net_WGCNA_H3K27ac_merged_by_1kb_sp5.Rds")
)
saveRDS(
  net_me3, file.path(output_dir, "net_WGCNA_H3K27me3_merged_by_1kb_sp9.Rds")
)
```


## Grey-module refinement and curated naming

The archived annotation code cuts hierarchical row dendrograms into 14 ATAC, 20 AC and 9 ME3 groups, then applies the manual labels below. This differs from the manuscript wording “k-means”; no k-means fit is substituted here. Cluster-number labels depend on the original input ordering. Final supplied assignments remain authoritative until a deliberate rerun is compared by interval ID. This section reads the original raw ATAC count matrix independently and does not require a new network fit.

```{r grey-module-refinement, eval=isTRUE(params$run_refinement)}

library(edgeR)
library(pheatmap)
output_dir <- file.path(REPO, "objects", "WGCNA", "recomputed")
dir.create(output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!exists("atac_counts")) {
  raw <- read.table(
    file.path(
      REPO, "data", "upstream", "WGCNA", "WGCNA_input_data", "atac_idr_peaks_merged_uniform-mm10.tsv"
    ),
    header = TRUE
  )
  atac_counts <- as.matrix(raw[, 5:24])
  storage.mode(atac_counts) <- "numeric"
  rownames(atac_counts) <- paste(raw$chrom, raw$start, raw$end, sep = "_")
}
catalog_dir <- file.path(REPO, "data", "upstream", "final_tables")
catalogs <- lapply(
  c(
    ATAC = "Supp_Table_1_ATAC_master.csv",
    AC = "Supp_Table_2_AC_master.csv",

    ME3 = "Supp_Table_3_ME3_master.csv"
  ),
  function(x) read.csv(
    file.path(catalog_dir, x),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)

# ATAC: the source refinement starts from the original raw-count table.  Match
# initial saved WGCNA assignments by stable interval ID.
atac_catalog <- catalogs$ATAC
atac_log_cpm <- edgeR::cpm(
  edgeR::DGEList(counts = atac_counts),
  log = TRUE,
  prior.count = 1
)
initial_colors <- setNames(atac_catalog$colors_ATAC_SP6, atac_catalog$ID)
grey_ids <- intersect(
  rownames(atac_log_cpm),
  names(initial_colors)[initial_colors ==
    "grey" & !is.na(initial_colors)]
)
atac_grey_matrix <- atac_log_cpm[grey_ids, , drop = FALSE]
atac_grey_heatmap <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  atac_grey_matrix,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  cutree_rows = 14,

  show_rownames = FALSE,
  silent = TRUE
)
atac_split <- cutree(
  as.hclust(atac_grey_heatmap$tree_row),
  k = 14
)
atac_split_names <- c(
  "P2_specific", "grey", "P2_specific", "Weak_late", "Weak_late", "Constitutive_weak",
  "RBP_specific", "grey", "Constitutive_strong", "Weak_middle", "grey", "grey",
  "grey", "grey"
)
atac_refinement <- data.frame(
  ID = names(atac_split),
  grey_ATAC_resplit = atac_split_names[atac_split]
)

# Histone grey modules use log2(FPKM + 1), column scaling and complete-linkage
# Euclidean row clustering (pheatmap defaults).
refine_histone_grey <- function(catalog, initial_color_column, k, labels) {
  selected <- catalog[!is.na(catalog[[initial_color_column]]) &
    catalog[[initial_color_column]] == "grey", , drop = FALSE]
  values <- as.matrix(
    selected[, grep("_fpkm$", names(selected)),
      drop = FALSE]
  )
  rownames(values) <- selected$ID
  values <- log2(values + 1)
  values <- values[apply(values, 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  clustered <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
    values,
    scale = "column",
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_cols = FALSE,
    cutree_rows = k,

    show_rownames = FALSE,
    silent = TRUE
  )
  split <- cutree(clustered$tree_row, k = k)
  data.frame(
    ID = names(split),
    Refined_label = labels[split]
  )
}
me3_refinement <- refine_histone_grey(
  catalogs$ME3,
  "colors_ME3_SP9",
  k = 9,
  labels = c(
    "grey", "Constitutive_medium", "Weak_late", "Constitutive_weak", "Constitutive_strong",
    "Weak_late", "grey", "grey", "grey"
  )
)
ac_refinement <- refine_histone_grey(
  catalogs$AC,
  "colors_AC_SP5",
  k = 20,
  labels = c(
    "Weak_late_VZ", "Grey", "Grey", "Weak_early_VZ", "Weak_early_VZ", "Constitutive_strong_1",
    "Strong_late_1", "Strong_late_2", "Weak_VZ", "Weak_VZ", "Constitutive_strong_2",
    "Grey", "Weak_early_VZ", "Grey", "Grey", "Grey", "Grey", "Grey", "Strong_late_2",
    "Grey"
  )
)
saveRDS(
  list(ATAC = atac_refinement, AC = ac_refinement, ME3 = me3_refinement),

  file.path(output_dir, "grey_refinement.rds")
)

# The curated dictionary maps biological labels to manuscript names; it is not
# another clustering operation.
module_dictionary <- read.csv(
  file.path(REPO, "data", "upstream", "Module_renaming_dictionary.csv"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

## Checkpoint-based figure export

The sections below use the verified saved results. Rerun outputs above are written separately and do not replace these inputs automatically.

## Load final network objects

No network fitting or recomputation of topological overlap occurs here.

```{r load-final-network-objects-2}
paths <- list.files(
  file.path(REPO, "data/upstream/WGCNA/WGCNA_objects"),
  pattern = "[.]Rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
stopifnot(
  length(paths) == 3
)
nets <- setNames(
  lapply(paths, readRDS),
  sub("[.]Rds$", "", basename(paths))
)
summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    names(nets),
    function(n) {
      x <- nets[[n]]
      data.frame(
        Network = n,
        Features = length(x$colors),

        Modules = length(unique(x$colors)),
        Samples = nrow(x$MEs)
      )
    }
  )
)
print(summary)
save_object(nets, "WGCNA/final_networks")
write.csv(
  summary, file.path(REPO, "reports/WGCNA_checkpoint_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Saved module eigengenes

Diagnostic checkpoint heatmaps retain the saved eigengene values; they are not replacements for the manuscript module-median plots.

```{r saved-module-eigengenes-3}
for (n in names(nets)) {
  m <- t(as.matrix(nets[[n]]$MEs))
  export_heatmap(
    m, paste0("WGCNA/", n, "_eigengenes"),
    width = 8,
    height = 6,
    zscore = TRUE,
    note = "Saved WGCNA eigengenes, row standardized for display; diagnostic only"
  )
}
```
